solutions.check: 28 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 27 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Soldiers beginning to show practical ingenuity

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's corps of soldiers
a beginning is a source, where something springs from

explanation.surface: Troops starting out show they can improvise in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' looks like a verb with 'to show'; it is a noun giving SOURCE, and 'to show' only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Resource is the knack of finding quick, workable ways out of difficulties, i.e. practical ingenuity.

clue.text: Outrageous suggestion, exposed originally in salesmen's lies

indicators.note: the initials are set inside the salesmen

parts.note: reps are sales representatives

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen's fibs contain an outlandish claim that's been unmasked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes O, S, E from Outrageous, suggestion, exposed; 'in' sets them in REPS. 'lies' is the verb: rests.
explanation.definitionFit: Reposes is a verb meaning rests or reclines, as someone stretched out on a couch does.

clue.text: Display work of art — an outstanding example

parts.note: to show is to display
a piece is a single work of art, music or writing

explanation.surface: An exhibited artwork is the best of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is the finest item, the exemplar put forward to impress.

clue.text: Discover a foreign land

parts.note: un is French for a, the indefinite article in a foreign tongue
earth is land, the ground

explanation.surface: Explorers find an overseas country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a foreign' asks for 'a' in another language: French UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up or bring to light is to discover something hidden.

clue.text: Reduced rake-off away from London

parts.note: a rake-off is a share or cut of the profits
going down means leaving London, the traditional direction away from the capital

explanation.surface: A smaller commission is taken outside the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: By British railway convention you go up to London and down when leaving it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut down means reduced in size or amount, trimmed.

clue.text: Retiring in two ways

parts.note: retiring can mean shy and unassuming, or holding back from showing off; one word covers both kinds of reticence

explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is unassuming and shy, and also avoids immodesty in dress or claims, both senses of being self-effacing.

clue.text: Calumnies disseminated about men

indicators.note: disseminated means scattered, so the letters of calumnies are spread and reassembled

explanation.surface: Slanders spread concerning males.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disseminated' rearranges CALUMNIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Masculine describes what pertains to the male sex, so it is an adjective meaning concerning males.

clue.text: He hesitates to obtrude, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of obtrude may come in some other order

explanation.surface: A man holds back from pushing himself forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OBTRUDE; 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsure, wavering over whether to believe, is a sceptic who hesitates.

clue.text: Iron hand required in prison in rebellion

parts.note: stir is slang for jail
R is short for right, as in the right hand
up in arms, rebels are said to be up

explanation.surface: A firm grip is needed among inmates who are rioting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like a hand of iron; it is the stirrup iron of a saddle. 'required in' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup iron is the metal foothold hanging from a saddle, so riders call it simply an iron.

clue.text: Qualities needed on the stage

definitions.meaning: attributes or characteristics of a thing
theatre objects used by actors, called props for short

explanation.surface: Attributes a theatre production cannot do without.
explanation.definitionFit: Characteristics of a substance are its attributes; in the theatre the objects handled on set are also called by this word, shortened to props.

clue.text: In the long run it covers one

indicators.note: the words run it cover, or hold within them, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Over time, something stretches to include a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the long' merely sets up the phrase 'in the long run'; the letters sit across 'run it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing counted as one.

clue.text: Wood was once thought to be a material with very little resistance

definitions.text: Wood was once thought to be
definitions.meaning: Sir Henry Wood, founder of the London Proms concerts, was reckoned a superb orchestra leader

definitions.text: a material with very little resistance
definitions.meaning: a substance that carries electric current with almost no electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Timber was formerly believed to be a near-perfect electrical medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' looks like timber, a material; it is Sir Henry Wood, the conductor who founded the BBC Proms concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant orchestra leader may be hailed as super; physics uses the same compound for a substance passing current with no resistance.

clue.text: Measure taken by governor together with new king

parts.note: a step is a measure taken to achieve something
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: A ruler's representative acts jointly with a freshly crowned monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: HE, His Excellency, is the formal style of a governor or ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen was a twelfth-century English monarch, so the name is an example of a king.

clue.text: Topping technique

definitions.meaning: British slang for killing someone, especially by hanging
the manner or skill of performing, as a pianist's

explanation.surface: Excellent method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like British slang for excellent; here it is slang for killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting to death is the judicial sense; a performer's skill in delivery is the other sense of the same word.

clue.text: Upset, purist daughter cracked up

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

indicators.note: the word purist is broken into pieces, its letters reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A stickler's daughter, distressed, has a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked up' tempts as the definition (laughed, or broke down); it is the anagram sign for 'purist', and 'Upset' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset plans is to throw them into disorder, the same as to disrupt them.

clue.text: State sailing centre with connections to public services

parts.note: UT is the postal abbreviation for Utah, a US state

indicators.note: the centre of sailing is its middle three letters

parts.note: ties are links or connections

explanation.surface: A yachting hub in some state has links to public utilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes ILI, the middle three of SAILING. Utilities are gas, water and electricity suppliers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas, water and power suppliers are collectively utilities, services provided for the public.

clue.text: Worried, as food's beginning to get spoiled by rot

indicators.note: the beginning of the word food's is its opening letter

parts.note: to ret flax or hemp is to soak it until it rots, so retted means rotted

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious because their groceries are starting to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: To RET is to soak flax so it rots; 'to get' only links the opening F to RETTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretted is a past tense meaning fussed anxiously, the same as worried.

clue.text: Strike boy in a fury

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: A lad in a temper lashes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links; RAMPAGE is the noun, a violent frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a violent outburst, a frenzy of rage.

clue.text: Escort put into a new suit

definitions.meaning: to take someone out on a date, or accompany them
in bridge, a bid forcing partner to bid a different suit

explanation.surface: A companion is fitted with a fresh outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing; in the card game bridge, a take-out double asks partner to bid another suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone on an outing is to take them out; in bridge, the same phrase means a bid that removes partner from their suit.

clue.text: Parcel I sent out in duplicate

indicators.note: the letters of parcel and I are dispatched and come back reordered

explanation.surface: A package is posted in two copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' rearranges PARCELI.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy of an original, such as an exact reproduction of a painting, is a duplicate.

clue.text: Absconded to appear on stage in the capital

parts.note: ran away, fled
actors go on when they enter the stage

explanation.surface: Someone fled to perform in a theatre in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links; Rangoon (now Yangon) was the capital of Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon was the seat of government of Burma, its chief city.

clue.text: Game permit, say, over a particular period

indicators.note: say signals that the word for permit is wanted only as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: to pass is to permit, as in passing a bill
a time is a particular period

explanation.surface: A gaming licence covers a certain period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives PAS, sounding like the word for permit; 'over' is only a link here, though it tempts as a reversal sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is a hobby or recreation, such as a game played for fun.

clue.text: Articles written about churchman wind up in the supplements

indicators.note: the two articles are set down around the other pieces

parts.note: A and A are two indefinite articles
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a clergyman's degree
to wind up is to end

explanation.surface: Columns about a cleric conclude in the appendices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' puts the two articles round the other pieces; 'in' links to the definition. DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the usual crossword churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are additions at the end of a book, its appendices.

clue.text: Decide to come to terms with a person's thinking

parts.note: to make up after a quarrel is to be reconciled, to come to terms
one's is the impersonal possessive, meaning any person's
the mind is the faculty of thinking

explanation.surface: Settling a matter means accepting what someone else thinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces; MAKE UP is the reconciling sense, not cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a firm decision is an idiom for settling your thoughts, choosing at last.

clue.text: Service return takes love game

indicators.note: a return sends the abbreviation back the other way, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
love is nil in tennis, written as the round letter O

explanation.surface: A tennis return wins a love game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns RAF to FAR; 'takes' adds O. Faro is an old gambling card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is a card game for gambling, popular in the Wild West.

clue.text: Infliction of punishment

definitions.meaning: the act of laying a burden or tax on someone
in British schools, a written task set as a penalty, such as lines

explanation.surface: Laying on a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing a burden is an infliction; and in British schools a set of lines given as a penalty carries the same name.

clue.text: The goddess in the mountain stirred

indicators.note: the goddess's name is placed inside the word for a mountain

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and mischief

explanation.surface: A deity inside a peak was agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is a Scottish mountain (Ben Nevis); ATE is the Greek goddess of ruin. 'stirred' is the definition, as eggs are beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten eggs or batter have been whisked, stirred vigorously.

clue.text: Reused an unconventional submarine

indicators.note: unconventional suggests an unusual arrangement of reused and an

explanation.surface: Recycled parts make an odd submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconventional' rearranges REUSEDAN. 'submarine' is the adjective, below the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means beneath the surface of the sea.
